# Apex Flow Web Scraper

> Convert accessible public web pages, PDF and DOCX documents into clean Markdown. Hosted API with prepaid credits, or open-source self-hosting. Built by Apex Flow Labs. Python package version 0.11.0; hosted launch 6 November 2026.

## What it does
- Converts pages to Markdown with headings, GFM tables, fenced code with language, absolute links; removes navigation, cookie banners and hidden elements.
- Renders JavaScript pages in an isolated Brave browser, with screenshots on request.
- For public dynamic pages, runs up to 8 declarative click/wait/scroll actions in one rendered request. Actions are bounded, cannot run user-supplied scripts or submit forms, and do not retain login state.
- Reads PDF, DOCX, RSS/Atom feeds and JSON.
- Data packages (hosted, 1 credit an answer): POST /v1/packages/housing {region, quarters} returns a US metro's house price index, one-year and five-year change and quarterly series from the Federal Housing Finance Agency (public domain; an index, not dollar prices); POST /v1/packages/npr {topic, limit} returns NPR headlines with links. GET /v1/packages lists them. MCP tools: house_prices, npr_news.
- Store watch (hosted, 1 credit per 250 products read): POST /v1/stores/track {store} saves a snapshot of a Shopify store's public catalog and returns what changed since the last one (new, price_drop, price_rise, sold_out, restocked, activity, removed); POST /v1/stores/rising {store, days, limit} ranks products by those changes (free; a change signal, not sales or revenue); GET /v1/stores lists tracked stores; POST /v1/stores/forget {store} deletes one. Free trial tracks 3 stores, paid plans 50. MCP tools: track_store, rising_products, tracked_stores.
- Scheduled monitoring (paid plans, explicit consent required): POST /v1/monitors with {url, webhook_url, interval_seconds, confirm_recurring:true}; minimum interval 3,600 seconds, maximum 30 days. One credit per successful plain-page check; failed reads are refunded. First success establishes a baseline; later content changes send HMAC-signed HTTPS events. Scheduled checks obey robots.txt, use public-address DNS validation, do not follow redirects, and pause on inactive entitlement or exhausted credits. Per-plan monitor-record limits, including paused records: Pass 5, Starter 10, Growth 100, Scale 500. MCP tools: create_monitor, list_monitors, pause_monitor, resume_monitor, delete_monitor, monitor_events. Verification guide: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/monitoring.html.
- Firecrawl-compatible async batches accept optional signed lifecycle webhooks in POST /v2/batch/scrape: started, page, and completed events; event filtering and metadata; public HTTPS callbacks on port 443; stable event IDs; HMAC signatures and bounded retries. The signing secret is returned once. Delivery is at-least-once, so receivers should deduplicate by event ID. Page callback bodies over 128 KiB are summarized; retrieve full results through batch status.
- Maps sites (robots.txt, nested and gzip sitemaps), crawls with durable jobs, change tracking with diffs.
- Owned full-text search (SQLite FTS5, BM25) over everything scraped.
- JSON-Schema extraction using DeepSeek first, OpenRouter second.
- MCP tools for agents: fetch, map, crawl, search, compare.
- Crawls and maps obey robots.txt; all requests obey Crawl-delay. A page requested by exact address is read even where robots.txt disallows it (receipt.robots_txt is then disallowed_read_on_request). A refused live read returns the Internet Archive copy by default, labelled; send "fallback":"none" for the error instead.
- Fetches public addresses only.

## Measured results (dated; not a current head-to-head)
- Latest Apex-only run, current 0.11.0 branch code (22 Nov 2026): 27/30 URLs fetched, 83/94 reference checks passed, median 1.16 s, with rendering disabled. Two URLs were robots-denied and one returned an HTTP error. Seven failed checks depend on JavaScript rendering; four reference checks use dated headlines that changed. All other checks passed. This is not a Firecrawl head-to-head; see BENCHMARK-2026-11-22.md.
- The comparable Firecrawl run is from 5 Nov 2026, not the current release: on 24 URLs with hand-scored reference checks, Apex 0.2.0 scored 91/93 and Firecrawl scored 85/93. Firecrawl returned 30/30 pages while Apex returned 26/30 on that run. The benchmark has not been rerun against current Firecrawl, so these numbers are historical evidence only, not a current superiority claim. See BENCHMARK-2026-11-05.md and tests/benchmark/.

## Hosted service and limits
- Hosted API: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/v1. OpenAPI 3.1: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/openapi.json. Human enrollment: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/trial.html. Free trial: 1,000 credits once, subject to network and daily capacity. Project Pass: $5 once for 35,000 credits valid for 30 days. Monthly plans: $15 for 110,000; $79 for 850,000; $299 for 3,750,000 credits. Plain pages cost 1, rendered pages 3, AI extraction 150 more. No automatic overages.
- Hosted: page scraping, JavaScript rendering and bounded click/wait/scroll actions, CSS field extraction, parallel batches of up to 10 URLs (pages at once: 2 on the trial, 6 on Pass and Starter, 12 on Growth, 20 on Scale), change tracking, durable scheduled monitoring, sitemap mapping, and account-scoped search over your latest scraped URLs (100 on the trial, 1,000 on paid plans). Actions run only within the current request and do not preserve browser or login sessions. A nonempty map costs 1 credit; saved-page search costs no credits.
- Hosted responses: 256 KiB per response. Longer documents are returned in consecutive parts (pagination.next_page; request with page). Concurrent page scrapes per account: 2 on the trial, 6 on Pass and Starter, 12 on Growth, 20 on Scale. Shared service limits: twenty active page scrapes and two simultaneous browser renders. Source crawl delays apply. Attempts, including failures, are capped at twice the plan's credits per period. Failed scrapes return reserved credits.
- AI extraction on paid plans: add extract {schema, prompt} to a scrape for 150 extra credits; result.extracted holds data, valid and errors. CSS recipes are free on every plan. Documentation: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html.

## Crawl a site
- POST /v1/crawl {url, limit} starts a background crawl of one site's own pages and returns an id. Page limits: 10 trial, 100 Pass and Starter, 500 Growth, 1,000 Scale. GET /v1/crawl/{id}?offset=N returns status and pages; follow next_offset until null. Each page costs 1 or 3 credits; failed pages are free. MCP: crawl_site then crawl_status.
- Python client: rainbo_scrape.hosted_client.Apex. Node client: sdk/node/hosted.mjs in the repository.

## For agents: change tracking, errors and usage
- Change tracking: every scrape response includes change.status (new, unchanged or changed) compared with the copy this account read last. Add "diff" to outputs to receive only the changed lines and the source receipt, without the page body. MCP tool: check_changes(urls).
- Errors are JSON with error, a stable code (invalid_key, insufficient_credits, inactive_plan, rate_limited, invalid_request, timeout, source_failed) and retryable. A 402 includes credits_left and buy_url; show buy_url to the user. A 429 includes retry_after seconds. MCP tool errors carry the same fields.
- Every response carries X-Credits-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Request-Id. GET /v1/usage returns plan, limits, renewal date and 14 days of daily usage.

- Context budgets: every scrape reply includes estimated_tokens. Set max_tokens (200-60000) to receive a page in consecutive parts that each fit the budget; follow pagination.next_page with page.
- Archive copy: when a live read of a named page fails because the site refused, errored or removed the page, the reply is the latest Internet Archive copy, labelled in result.archive with captured, snapshot_url and reason, and result.warnings includes archived_copy. Send "fallback":"none" to receive the error instead. Crawls use archive copies only with "fallback":"archive".

## Not claimed
- No CAPTCHA solving or bot-wall evasion; sites behind bot walls, such as glassdoor.com, block live reads. The archive copy (on by default for named pages) returns a dated Internet Archive copy where one exists.
- POST /v1/search and the search_saved MCP tool search only this account's previously scraped pages. Whole-web /v1/websearch and web_search MCP are separate and require the service operator to configure exactly one provider: Brave Search, Tavily Search or Exa Search. If several provider keys are configured, set APEX_SEARCH_PROVIDER to choose one; ambiguous setup keeps web_search disabled. Successful searches cost 130 credits with Brave, 210 with Tavily basic search, or 180 with Exa for up to 10 requested results plus 25 credits per requested result above 10. Successful empty results are billed; failed provider calls refund the reservation. Provider charges are billed separately to the operator's provider account.
- We do not claim universal competitor superiority, the lowest price for every workload, or guaranteed availability on every source.

## Agent setup
Official MCP Registry entry: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/io.github.Apexflowlabsllc%2Fapex-flow-web-scraper/versions/latest
Set up Codex CLI, Claude Code or VS Code: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html#agents
Remote MCP: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/v1/mcp (Streamable HTTP, Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY). Core tools: scrape_page, scrape_batch, check_changes, create_monitor, list_monitors, pause_monitor, resume_monitor, delete_monitor, monitor_events, map_site, crawl_site, crawl_status, search_saved and credit_balance. Additional tools include house_prices, npr_news, track_store, rising_products and tracked_stores. web_search is available only when the service operator configures a search provider. Stdio clients: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html#agents. Enrollment requires a human. A portable Agent Skill with a standard-library Python CLI is prepared in the current branch; its one-command install becomes available after merge to the public default branch: npx skills add Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper --skill apex-flow-web-scraper. The npm multi-client installer also requires package publication; when available, `apex-flow-web-scraper doctor` will verify authenticated MCP tool discovery without running a scrape or using credits.
Grok CLI: add a remote server to ~/.grok/config.toml with url=https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/v1/mcp and an Authorization header value of Bearer ${APEX_SCRAPER_API_KEY}. Set that environment variable before launching Grok; Grok expands it when loading headers, so the API key is not stored in the config. Verify with grok mcp doctor apex_flow_web_scraper. Official reference: https://docs.x.ai/build/features/mcp-servers. The installer can configure this target individually with `setup --client grok` after npm publication.

## Direct AI API integrations
- OpenAI Responses API with remote MCP: https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/examples/openai-responses-mcp.py
- Anthropic Messages API with remote MCP: https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/examples/anthropic-messages-mcp.py
- Google ADK / Gemini with remote MCP: https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/examples/google-adk-mcp.py
- xAI / Grok native Python SDK with remote MCP: https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/examples/xai-native-mcp.py
- xAI / Grok Responses API with remote MCP: https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/examples/xai-responses-mcp.py. Both examples allow only scrape_page and keep both API keys in the caller's environment. xAI's Responses API currently does not support require_approval; a call can consume xAI tokens and Apex credits. xAI Remote MCP reference: https://docs.x.ai/developers/tools/remote-mcp
- Vercel AI SDK 7 with the official @ai-sdk/mcp client: server-side Streamable HTTP example at https://github.com/Apexflowlabsllc/apex-flow-web-scraper/blob/main/sdk/node/examples/vercel-ai-sdk-mcp.mjs. It passes Apex's discovered MCP tools to generateText and keeps both Apex and model-provider credentials in the server environment.

## Usage
Python: `from rainbo_scrape import scrape; scrape("https://example.com").markdown`
CLI: `rainbo-scrape fetch https://example.com`

For a smaller REST or MCP scrape response, select outputs such as ["markdown"] or ["data", "evidence"]. Source receipts and validation warnings are retained when available.

- Shopify store tracker API (catalog changes and rising products): https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/shopify-store-tracker.html
- Firecrawl public monthly prices checked 21 November 2026: Free 1,000 credits/month; Hobby $19 (5,000); Standard $99 (100,000); Growth $399 (500,000); Scale $749 (1,000,000). Annual billing is listed at $16/$83/$333/$599. Credit definitions and plan features differ, so these are not equivalent-workload guarantees. Source: https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing. Firecrawl also has higher service concurrency, broader search/extraction/browser APIs, enterprise controls, and a much larger distribution ecosystem.
- Dated price comparisons with tradeoffs, read 13 November 2026: ScrapingBee https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/scrapingbee-alternative.html; ScraperAPI https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/scraperapi-alternative.html; Scrapfly https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/scrapfly-alternative.html; ZenRows https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/zenrows-alternative.html; Apify https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/apify-alternative.html
- Self-hosted: read pages you are signed in to through your own browser profile on your own machine (rainbo-scrape login, then fetch --signed-in). Not part of the hosted API.
